en: The Lotus Sutra, Chapter Thirty: The Bodhisattva Maṅgala. The Buddha said:
"The earth is twenty billion *yojana* deep. Beneath the earth is moisture, twenty billion *yojana* deep.
Beneath the moisture is golden grain, twenty billion *yojana* deep. Golden grain...
Below is the Diamond [Realm] (vajra),
twenty billion *li* in depth.
Beneath the Diamond Realm is a great body of water.
It is eighty billion *li* deep.
Beneath the water is an infinite great wind,
eighty-five billion *li* deep.
The firmness of the heavens and earth maintains them so that they do not fall.
When the heavens and earth are about to perish, seven suns appear;
when two suns appear, they halt in their tracks and cease to move.
All the waters from the various sources will become parched and exhausted.
When three suns appear, all the rivers will completely dry up.
When four suns appear, the great rivers and streams will all be completely dried up.
When five suns appear, the great ocean dries up completely.
When six suns appear, the world becomes parched like a potter’s kiln,
as if smoke were rising from a burning fire.
When seven suns arise, the entire world is completely consumed by fire and burned away;
Mount Sumeru and all the myriad things beneath heaven are utterly destroyed.
The fierce heat of that fire burns upward, incinerating the various heavens until the six heavens are entirely exhausted.
That fire, blazing with intense heat, reaches as far as the fifteenth heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven.
Among the people of the world, those who have performed much merit die and are reborn above in the fifteenth heaven.
Those with little merit are reborn in other regions and lands;
the offenders within the hells of this world are all reborn in the hells of other regions to undergo their retribution.
After heaven and earth have been consumed by fire, there arises a great wind.
Coming from another direction, they hold clouds that rise up to the seventh heaven and rain down drops as large as chariot wheels.
Thus the rain fell for billions of koṭis of years,
and the water rose until it reached the seventh Brahma-heaven;
then great winds arose from all four directions above, severing the flow so that it did not overflow.
A wind arises and agitates that water for hundreds of thousands of millions of years,
until the water is finally diminished.
Then, another wind arises.
It is named Pure Adornment;
it stirs its waters so that thick foam arises upon the waves, which transforms into the seven treasures.
When the construction of the sixth palace, that of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, first began,
the waters gradually receded.
A wind called "Pure Adornment" arose and blew upon the water foam, transforming it into the seven precious jewels.
Next, the fifth celestial palace of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven is formed;
as it gradually diminishes,
the wind of Pure Adornment arises and blows upon the water-foam, transforming it into the seven precious gems.
Next, the fourth Tuṣita celestial palace is formed.
As the waters gradually recede,
the Wind of Pure Adornment arises and blows upon the water-foam, transforming it into the seven precious jewels.
Next, the third palace of the Yāma Heaven is formed.
As the waters gradually recede,
the Pure Adornment Wind arises and blows upon the water foam, transforming it into the seven precious jewels.
Gold, silver, crystal, and lapis lazuli constitute Mount Sumeru in the midst of the heavens,
rising three million three hundred and sixty thousand *li* in height.
The waters gradually recede.
The Wind of Pure Adornment arises and blows upon the water foam, transforming it into the seven precious jewels.
At the summit of Mount Sumeru, the second palace of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven is formed.
As the waters gradually recede,
the Wind of Pure Adornment arises and blows upon the water-foam, transforming it into the seven precious jewels.
At the midpoint of Mount Sumeru, rising up on four peaks, the palaces of the Four Heavenly Kings are constructed.
The waters gradually recede.
A wind called Pure Adornment arises and blows upon the water foam, transforming it into the seven treasures;
gold and crystal become the suns.
The moon is made of white silver and lapis lazuli,
as are the palaces of the various honored deities and the constellations;
as the waters gradually recede, these appear.
The firm wind arises and blows upon the water-foam,
transforming it into jewels and forming ten jewel-mountains;
the first is the Gold Mountain.
The second is the Silver Mountain;
the third is the Lapis Lazuli Mountain;
the fourth is the Agate Mountain.
Fifth is the Musāragalva Mountain;
sixth is the Amber Mountain;
seventh is the Crystal Mountain.
Eighth is Crystal Mountain;
ninth is White Jade Mountain;
tenth is Purple Gold Mountain.
Furthermore, he constructed twenty-eight celestial palaces for the earth-dwelling devas,
adorned with seven kinds of primary jewels and one hundred and twenty kinds of miscellaneous gems.
The *āśraya-vāyu* (abiding wind) arises and blows upon the water-foam, transforming it into the Cakravāḍa mountains.
The Great Cakravāḍa mountains encircle the trichiliocosm.
Next, the *aniñjya-vāyu* (immovable wind) arises and blows upon the clear water, forming the oceans.
The extremely turbid coarse froth transforms into stone mountains;
the murky waters form the four great continents and the lands of the eighty thousand small cities and territories.
Once the earth-city has been established, the earth naturally produces medicinal herbs.
Subsequently, a person from the fifteenth heaven gradually descends and dwells among the six heavens of the desire realm.
Later, they descend again to the ground;
some eat the fungi of the earth.
Having eaten these fungi, they become greedily attached to their flavor.
Their bodies became heavy so that they could no longer fly;
their merit exhausted, they became worldly humans and were no longer possessed of radiance.
The human lifespan was immeasurable years.
When the terrestrial fungi had completely perished,
the flavor of the earth subsequently appeared.
The people took it and ate together;
their lifespan lasted for many thousands of millions of years.
Then, the essence of the earth (pṛthivī-rasa) was completely exhausted.
Thereafter, the earth-fertility (pṛthivī-parpaṭaka) arose.
The people took its yellow substance and ate it.
After their lifespan had reached several tens of millions of years, [the fertility vanished].
When the earth-fertility had been completely exhausted,
naturally occurring non-glutinous rice grew;
the people all ate this natural non-glutinous rice together.
After eating the non-glutinous rice,
those whose minds were inclined toward few desires transformed into male forms,
while those whose minds were inclined toward many desires transformed into female forms.
After their bodies have transformed into male and female forms,
they immediately give rise to lustful attachment and engage in sexual intercourse in secluded places.
This occurs when the merit and lifespan of those in the fifteenth heaven above come to an end.
Descending into the womb of a woman as a fetus,
it takes three hundred days to become a human being;
from this point onward, one brings forth sons and nurtures daughters.
They shall intermarry with one another,
their six relations shall become steadfast,
and they shall eat non-glutinous rice.
At that time, the human lifespan was several million years.
Although they all possessed minds prone to contention,
even while partaking of things that appeared spontaneously, they would still steal from and plunder one another.
They beat and struck one another until the non-glutinous rice was completely exhausted,
whereupon wild rice grew spontaneously.
They then divided the territory and demarcated the boundaries,
each guarding their own portion. However,
because there were foolish people who secretly robbed one another, it could not be restrained.
Thereupon, the royal law was established;
the high ministers and hundred officials inspected one another,
rewarding the good and punishing the evil.
The state was governed with legal and political order, and the people were not oppressed.
Each person contributed their own clothing and food to provide for the king.
At that time, the human life span was five hundred years.
From that time forward, they began to strike and jostle one another;
those who failed to repay their debts were immediately transformed into the bodies of animals,
drinking water and eating grass.
While alive, they are made to carry heavy burdens;
when dead, their skins are flayed.

These include elephants, horses, oxen, sheep, donkeys, mules, camels, pigs, dogs, chickens, cranes, geese, ducks, bears, brown bears, tigers, leopards, jackals, wolves, elk, *mùchǔ* (a type of deer), *zhānglù* (a type of deer), gazelles, pheasants, and rabbits.
All are transformations of humans;
such manifestations are beyond counting.
At that time, those who were stingy and greedy among humans were immediately transformed into hungry ghosts.
He is forty li in height.
When he lifts his feet to walk, the joints of his limbs rub against one another,
producing a sound like that of five hundred chariots.
Their bellies are vast while their navels are like needles;
when they see food and drink, it transforms into glowing coals,
and when they see the Ganges, it transforms into pus and blood.
Wandering east and west in search of food, he enters Yangdong Cave.
A single mouthful of food enters his belly,
and all his hundred joints burst into flames.
Such suffering, affliction, and poisonous pain are beyond description.
At that time, people commit the ten unwholesome deeds:
killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, divisive speech, harsh speech, slanderous speech, covetousness, malice, and delusion.

Upon reaching the space between the two Iron Ring Mountains (Cakravāḍa), they shall be interrogated and punished within eighteen hells: First, the Hell of Boiling Cauldrons; Second, the Hell of Charcoal Embers; Third, the Hell of Mountain Blades;

Fourth, the Hell of Sword-Leaf Trees; Fifth, the Hell of Utter Darkness; Sixth, the Hell of Frozen Ice; Seventh, the Hell of the Fiery Chariot; Eighth, the Hell of Weapons; Ninth, the Hell of the Fire Wheel; Tenth, the Hell of Iron Spikes; Eleventh, the Hell of the Copper Pillar; Twelfth, the Hell of Boiling Excrement; Thirteenth, the Hell of Tongue Extraction; Fourteenth, the Hell of Nailing the Body; Fifteenth, the Hell of Spitting Fire; Sixteenth, the Hell of Drinking Molten Copper; Seventeenth, the Hell of Ignorance; Eighteenth, the Hell of the Fiery City. These are for those who have committed the ten evil deeds.
They all undergo punishment throughout these eighteen hells,
spending billions of years in each individual hell.
One day and one night in those hells is equivalent to one hundred and twenty thousand years in the human realm.
After such a long time,
they finally emerge,
only to enter among the animals once more.
For five hundred million years, they undergo the form of birds and beasts;
when their karmic retribution as animals is exhausted, they enter among the hungry ghosts for another five million years;
and when their karmic retribution as hungry ghosts is exhausted, they are reborn among the frontier tribes and barbarians.
They shall be defeated by kings and become slaves to others for five hundred lifetimes;
only then will their transgressions be exhausted.
Those who uphold the five precepts further obtain a human body;
those who practice the ten wholesome actions are reborn in the heavens;
and those who cultivate the Path attain the Path.
The Buddha said:
"To the north of Mount Sumeru lies the land named Uttarakuru;
its territory is four hundred thousand li square."
The human lifespan is one thousand years;
the body is four chi tall,
and the human face resembles the shape of the earth, being square.
On the trees grew garments and necklaces made of the seven precious gems;
from the earth naturally sprang non-glutinous rice,
its flavor like ambrosia.
Those who eat it remain free from illness;
there is no distinction between the noble and the lowly.
The inhabitants of that land are constant in their pursuit of their karmic tasks.
Furthermore, there are none who die prematurely.
The people of that land have no one to nurse their infants;
as soon as a child is born and falls to the ground, it is taken up by the roadside.
He causes the practitioner to extend his fingers and place them in his mouth to suck them;
after sucking them for seven days, he becomes a full-grown man and goes beneath the tree.
Looking up at the trees,
they see those whose bodies are adorned with necklaces and garments made of the seven precious gems;
there is no suffering from dyeing or the labor of pressing and smoothing the cloth.
Furthermore, there is no labor involved in cutting, tailoring,
or sewing. The people of that country are upright and virtuous beyond compare,
being the foremost among all those in the three continents.
If they encounter a woman, she becomes their wife;
if they encounter a man, he becomes their husband.
Those people possess a compassionate heart and do not kill living beings.
When the dragon kings send down rain, it rains exquisite flowers.
The people of that land take them to adorn themselves;
they are born without the need for mutual nourishment.
Upon death, they are not buried.
Great birds carry their corpses and place them in uninhabited lands;
their spirits ascend to heaven without passing through the evil realms.
By upholding the five precepts, one attains rebirth in that land. To the north of Mount Sumeru is where the sun rises;
to the west of the mountain is midday;
and to the south of the mountain is sunset.
At midnight in Shandong,
Mount Sumeru is three million three hundred and thirty-six thousand li high;
its shape is like that of a narrow-headed drum.
The lower extremity enters the water,
extending three million three hundred and sixty thousand *li* down to the adamantine foundation (*vajra-maṇḍala*).
From the summit to this lower extremity, the total height is six million seven hundred and twenty thousand *li*.
The height of the Lesser Iron Ring Mountains above the surface of the Lesser Ocean waters is six million seven hundred twenty-two thousand *li*;
their depth submerged within the ocean waters is also six million seven hundred twenty-two thousand *li*.
From its summit down to its base, it is one hundred thirty-four million four hundred thousand *li* in height.
This is Mount Sumeru, situated within these four continents and surrounded by the Lesser Iron Ring Mountains.
In the language of Qin, it is called Mount Kunlun.
It is composed of four precious substances;
its eastern face is of gold.
The western face is of white silver;
the southern face is of lapis lazuli;
the northern face is of crystal.
In the east there was gold;
the golden radiance illuminated the eastern realm of space, making it entirely the color of gold.
The sentient beings of that direction said, "It is a yellow heaven."
In the western direction was white silver.
The radiance of the white silver illuminated the void-realm of the western direction until it was entirely the color of white silver.
The sentient beings of that region said, "It is the White Heaven."
In the south is Vaiḍūrya.
The radiance of Vaiḍūrya illuminates the southern realm of empty space, making it entirely the color of Vaiḍūrya;
the sentient beings of this region call it the blue sky.
In the north is crystal;
the radiance of this crystal illuminates the heavens.
The radiance of these four jewels illuminates all directions.
All are identical in color and have no boundaries or shores.
All sentient beings are obscured by emptiness, clarity, turbidity, and cataracts, being hindered by form;
for this reason, it is called Mount Sumeru.
"Only those who have attained the divine eye can see it.
The Buddha said, "To the east of Mount Sumeru, there is a land called Pūrvavideha.
It is three hundred and twenty thousand li in breadth and length."
The land is perfectly circular;
the faces of its inhabitants resemble the shape of the terrain,
and their height is one zhang.
Six hundred and fifty years [passed].
Those people possessed a heart of compassion and refrained from killing living beings.
Heaven rained down various jewels, and food and clothing appeared spontaneously.
Those who uphold the five precepts shall be reborn in that land.
When the sun rises over the eastern side of Mount Sumeru,
it is midday on its northern side.
When the sun sets behind the mountains in the west, it is midnight on the southern slopes. The Buddha said:
"To the west of Mount Sumeru is the land called Aparagoyānī."
It is thirty-six hundred thousand li in circumference.
Its land is shaped like a half-moon,
and the faces of its inhabitants resemble the shape of the terrain.
Their height is two zhang;
their lifespan is two hundred and fifty years.
These people possess a compassionate heart and do not kill living beings.
The heavens rain down flower filaments, and clothing and food appear spontaneously.
Those who maintain the five precepts of middle grade shall be born in that land.
It is located to the west of Mount Sumeru, where the sun rises.
When it is midday on the south side of the mountain,
it is sunset on the east side,
and midnight on the north side. Thus spoke the Buddha.
The land south of Mount Sumeru is named Jambudvīpa.
It measures two hundred and eighty thousand li in breadth and length;
its surface is broad at the top and narrow at the bottom.
The faces of the people resemble the terrain.
The practices cultivated by the inhabitants of that land are not fixed,
and the retributions they receive do not remain constant.
The highest lifespan is one hundred and twenty years;
the middle lifespan is one hundred years;
the lowest lifespan is eighty years.
The upper body was twelve feet long;
the middle body was ten feet;
the lower body was eight feet.
There is little that emerges and much that diminishes; deceitful and false sentiments are few.
Regarding the mind of loving-kindness (*maitrī*), it relies solely on the power of food and does not arise spontaneously.
When it rains, the rain falls as clear and cool water.
To moisten the five grains, millet, fruits, and trees,
the Dragon King sends down rain without any distinction;
this continues until the end of the kalpa.
The people there are extremely wicked;
they grasp blades made of grass and immediately kill one another.
At that time, the lifespan will be five years;
all five grains will have completely perished,
and the reduction in the karmic actions of sentient beings will vary.
Those who uphold the five precepts in an inferior manner are born in this land.
When the sun rises over Mount Sumeru in the south,
it is midday on the eastern mountain.
When the sun sets behind the northern mountains, it is midnight behind the western mountains. The Buddha said:
"The sun is eighty-four thousand li from the earth."
The inner city was made of gold,
and the outer city was made of crystal.
For this reason, the world was always bright, and there were three roads for travel during the day.
In winter, the path travels south,
passing over ice mountains;
for this reason, the world is bitterly cold.
In spring and autumn, it travels the middle path;
therefore, the cold and warmth are moderate and balanced.
In summer, it travels the northern path.
Above the realm of humans,
three million three hundred and sixty thousand li further to the north,
lies the sun-essence known as the Golden Lotus Body.
Therefore, the world is intensely hot.
The city of the sun is exactly two thousand forty li in length and breadth.
The city walls are made of gold and crystal;
the lifespan of the people is two hundred and fifty years,
and their height is ten *li*.
Food and clothing appear spontaneously.
The Sun Deity emits a thousand rays of light that universally illuminate hundreds of thousands of lands;
within them there are also men and women.
By practicing the five precepts and the ten wholesome actions and lighting lamps to illuminate the Buddha, one cultivates these merits and attains birth among the suns. The Buddha said:
"The moon is eighty-four thousand *li* from the earth."
The inner city is made of white silver,
and the outer city is made of lapis lazuli.
When the moon first appears on the first day of its cycle, its silver surface turns toward people.
On the fifteenth day, it faces people directly;
for this reason, the moon is full and the world is brilliantly illuminated.
From the sixth day onward, its lapis lazuli surface turns toward people.
On the thirtieth day, it faces toward humans;
this is the great darkness of the world.
The moon-city is one thousand nine hundred and sixty li in length, breadth, height, and depth.
The city walls are made of white silver and lapis lazuli;
the lifespan of its inhabitants is two hundred and fifty years,
and their height is ten *li*.
Food and clothing are provided spontaneously.
Among them there are both men and women;
they practice the five precepts and the ten wholesome actions, and light lamps to illuminate the Buddhas.
By cultivating these merits, one attains birth within the moon. The Buddha said:
"As for the five planets:
the first is Jupiter (Venus) in the east."
In the south is the planet Mars; in the west, Venus;
in the north, Mercury;
and in the center, Saturn.
These are called the five planets.
They are of three grades: great, medium, and small.
A great planet is one hundred and twenty *li* in length and breadth.
The medium-sized stars are eighty *li* in extent,
and the small stars are forty *li*;
all have city walls and moats made of crystal.
It is eighty-four thousand *li* above the earth;
because it is turned by the Svarṇa wind, it does not fall. The Buddha said:
"In the heavens there are twenty-eight lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*)."
They preside over the four directions,
corresponding to the four seasons without ever failing their constant measure.
The seven lunar mansions of the eastern quarter are as follows:
Jiǎo, Kāng, Dǐ, Fáng, Xīn, Wěi,
and Jī are the seven lunar mansions of the south.
Jǐng, Guǐ, Liù, Xīng, Zhāng, Yì, and Zhěn are [the seven lunar mansions of the west].
The seven lunar mansions of the western quarter are Ascendant, Hand, Woman, Void, Peril, Chamber, and Opening.
The seven lunar mansions of the northern quarter are... [as above].
Quellou, Weilou, Miaolu, Bilu, Zilu, and Shenshu—now these sun, moon, and lunar mansions are all the palaces of the various devas, adorned with the seven treasures.
They abide in the profound void, revolving through the four seasons without losing their proper measure.
It is also sustained by five winds:
first, the sustaining wind;
second, the awaiting wind.
Third is the assisting wind;
fourth is the turning wind;
fifth is the circulating wind.
It was established so that [the world] would not fall downward.
Among the constellations, there is a human body ten *zhang* in height.
Their lifespan is two hundred and fifty years,
which corresponds to four million five hundred thousand years in the human realm.
Twenty-five human years constitute one day and one night among the Nakṣatra-devas.
Food and clothing were provided spontaneously;
his neck and back were bathed in sunlight;
and he traveled through the air with complete ease.
Among them are both men and women;
these are born there because they upheld the five precepts and the ten wholesome actions while in the human realm.
To the east, the palace of the Heavenly King of the East governs the midpoint of Mount Sumeru, where golden peaks soar upward.
It is one million six hundred and eighty thousand *li* from the earth.
To the east of Mount Sumeru is the Heavenly King named Dhṛtarāṣṭra;
in the Han language, this means "Governor of the Realm."
He is the lord of all gandharvas and piśāca spirits.
The life span of this Heavenly King who Governs the State is five hundred years,
which corresponds to nine million years in the human realm today.
Fifty human years constitute one day and night in the palace of the Four Heavenly Kings (Cāturmahārājakāyika).
Thirty such days constitute one month,
and twelve such months constitute one year.
Food and clothing are provided spontaneously.
Among them there are both men and women,
and their height is twenty *li*.
By practicing the five precepts and the ten wholesome actions, one attains birth therein.
The palace of the Southern Heavenly King, which governs the middle slope of Mount Sumeru,
is made of soaring lapis lazuli and stands sixty thousand *li* above the earth.
To the south of Mount Sumeru is the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka,
which in the Han language means "Growth.
He presides over all venomous dragons and pūtana demons.
The life span of the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka is five hundred years;
this corresponds to nine million years in the human realm.
Fifty years in the human realm constitute one day and night in the palace of the Four Heavenly Kings.
Thirty days constitute one month;
twelve months constitute one year.
Clothing and food are provided spontaneously.
Within it there are also men and women.
They are twenty *li* tall in stature.
Those who practice the five precepts and the ten wholesome deeds are reborn therein.
The palace of the Heavenly King of the Western Quarter is situated halfway up Mount Sumeru, where white silver rises upward.
It is one million six hundred and eighty thousand *li* from the ground.
To the west of Mount Sumeru is the Heavenly King named Virūḍhaka.
In the language of Han, he is called Nanguo (Difficult to Overcome). He presides over all the Kumbhāṇḍas and Pūtanas.
King Nanyu (Difficult Speech) has a lifespan of five hundred years.
At present, the human lifespan is nine million years.
Fifty human years constitute one day and night in the palace of the Four Heavenly Kings.
Thirty such days constitute one month.
Twelve months constitute one year.
Food and clothing appear spontaneously.
Among them, there are both men and women.
The inhabitants are twenty *li* in height.
Those who practice the five precepts and the ten wholesome actions are reborn therein.
The palace of the Northern Heavenly King (*Virūpākṣa*) is situated on the mid-slope of Mount Sumeru, where a crystal peak rises upward.
It is one million six hundred and eighty thousand *li* from the ground.
To the north of Mount Sumeru is the Heavenly King named Vaiśravaṇa;
in the Han language, he is called "Much-Hearing" (Duowen).
He is the lord of all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and pretas.
The lifespan of the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa is five hundred years,
which corresponds to nine million years in the human world.
Fifty human years constitute one day and night in the palace of the Four Heavenly Kings.
Thirty such days constitute one month,
and twelve such months constitute one year.
Food and clothing are provided spontaneously.
Among them there are both men and women,
each of whom is twenty li in height.
By practicing the five precepts and the ten wholesome actions, one attains birth therein.
Although the palaces of the Four Heavenly Kings possess the names of days, months, and years, they lack the actual forms of days, months, and years.
The reason for this is that the various devas in the palaces of the Four Heavenly Kings possess radiant light on their necks and backs,
which illuminates one another in succession.
There is neither day nor night;
it is perpetually bright and never dark.
If you wish to know the characteristics of this absence of day and night:
One need only observe the opening and closing of the lotus flowers to know it:
when the lotus blooms, it is called day;
when the flower closes, it is called night.
The four seasonal elements are in harmonious balance,
being neither cold nor hot;
this is true throughout all the successive tiers up to the Heaven of the Thirty-three.
However, their days, months, and years increase in length at double the rate and are not comparable [to ours].
Each of the Four Heavenly Kings governs one quarter of the world and regularly dispatches messengers on the eighth day of the month.
He traveled throughout the world,
observing and scrutinizing emperors, ministers, and subjects, as well as devas, nāgas, spirits, ghosts, and all classes of beings— whether winged, crawling, or wriggling—
and their thoughts and spoken words.
The body performs good and evil deeds;
the record of good is clear and the record of evil is distinct,
with every detail accurately distinguished down to the finest hair.
Those who have practiced good enter the Office of Heaven;
those who have committed evil deeds are said to be in the four dark chambers of humans.
On the fourteenth day, the Prince descends.
On the fifteenth day, the Four Heavenly Kings descended in person;
on the twenty-third day, they again dispatched messengers;
and on the twenty-ninth day, they again sent their princes.
On the thirtieth day, the Four Heavenly Kings descend once more;
the sun, moon, five planets, and twenty-eight lunar mansions,
along with all the devas within them, descend together.
He subtly observed the world’s emperors, ministers, subjects, dragons, spirits, and all sentient beings:
who among them was practicing filial piety toward their parents or reverently serving the Three Honored Ones?
One should uphold the Three Refuges, the Five Precepts, the Ten Wholesome Actions, and the Eightfold Fasting Observances;
erect stupas and fashion images to cultivate all manner of meritorious virtues;
and practice the Six Perfections along with loving-kindness and the four immeasurable states of mind.
Those who practice giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence,
single-minded concentration, and wisdom, and who nurture sentient beings through compassion, kindness, sympathetic joy, and equanimity,
shall have their names recorded and submitted to Śakra, Lord of the Devas.
Śakra, having received the letter, submitted it to the Heavenly Office below;
his lifespan was increased, and his years were fulfilled for a full hundred.
When he approached the end of his life, [he attained liberation].
Led by the celestial music and accompanied by a jeweled chariot,
five hundred heavenly maidens scattered flowers and burned incense as they came to welcome him, ascending with him to the palace of the Heavenly King in the heavens.
Their robes were dark and wondrous;
their food was of exquisite delicacies;
when they traveled, they soared through the void.
Dwelling in the flower-adorned palace,
his eyes beheld exquisite forms and his ears heard sublime melodies.
The mouth tastes a hundred flavors;
the nose smells wondrous fragrances;
the body wears patterned silks.
The mind roams through the pure realms;
the sustenance for this merit is the ten wholesome actions.
As for those who commit evil deeds—
Śakra, having received the letter, delivered it to King Yama of the Underworld;
King Yama immediately dispatched the five officials of hell to diminish their lifespans and seize their allotted years.
He was named Ming She (Famous Archer).
Soldiers of the hell guard him, surrounding him with iron chains;
what they see differs [from one another].
They are unable to speak;
each receives their own calamity or fortune according to what they have practiced.
It is impossible to escape by offering wealth or pleading for mercy.
Heaven does not perversely grasp;
it is impartial and straightforward, without duality.
One who commits a transgression shall receive its retribution.
By performing meritorious deeds, one attains the practice of the Path.
What one does oneself, one receives oneself;
it is not bestowed by another.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"The ten wholesome actions lead to birth in heaven; The five precepts result in a human body. The ten unwholesome actions cause one to fall into hell;
Violence leads to rebirth as an animal. Through patience one obtains an upright appearance; Through anger one becomes ugly."
Through giving, one attains great wealth; through stinginess and greed, one falls into poverty.
The second heaven is named Trāyastriṃśa, and its ruler is named Śakra Devānām Indra.
The four great ministers who guard the quarters are the Four Heavenly Kings.
As for the Heaven of the Thirty-three:
Śakra has thirty-two ministers;
together with the body of Śakra himself, there are thus the Thirty-three Heavens (Trāyastriṃśa).
When Śakra-devānām-indra sits upon his Maṇi-jewel palace, [the gods gather around him].
In front there were eight ministers;
behind there were eight ministers;
on the left there were eight ministers.
On the right side there are eight ministers;
since four times eight equals thirty-two, there are thus thirty-two assistant ministers.
As for the Three Dukes:
The Minister of Education (Situ), the Grand Master of Ceremonies (Kong), and the Grand Master of the Palace (Simagong).
As for the Nine Ministers: these are the eight Grand Secretaries (Shangshu) plus the Minister of Works (Xiaosan).
The messengers of the Eight Kings;
the Altar of the Soil on the left and the Altar of the Grain on the right;

The Left General and Right General;
the Front General and Rear General;

The Great King Pañcāla’s crown prince and his messengers,

King Śākya had a queen named Manoharā;
on both her left and right sides were eighty-four thousand attendants of exquisite beauty.
Upon her face, moreover, there were eighty-four thousand ornaments;
these ornaments were the most supreme among the thirty-two *nayuta* of celestial maidens belonging to Śakra.
The summit of Mount Sumeru is three million three hundred and sixty thousand *li* above the ground;
the summit is three million three hundred and sixty thousand *li* in length and breadth.
The city is named Priyadarśana (Joyful to Behold).
It is one million six hundred and eighty thousand *li* distant from the palaces of the Four Heavenly Kings.
Upon entering the ocean, the water is further deepened by three million three hundred and sixty thousand *li*.
Its lower roots are also equal in length and breadth.
It is three million three hundred and sixty thousand *li* in extent.
Its city, named Sudarśana, is adorned with the seven treasures;
the city is perfectly square in its length and breadth.
It is eighty-four thousand yojanas in extent.
In its center is the palace of Śakra, a palace made of the seven precious substances, furnished with carpets, rugs, gold beds, and jade desks;
its hangings are soft and fine.
These were spread upon it;
celestial silk and precious rugs served as a cushion for his body,
and garments of *karpāsa* cotton cloth were laid over them.
Naturally adorning his body were exquisite celestial garments of precious jewels,
which were draped over his head.
Adorned with pearl necklaces,
and with mani-jewels and *louchang* canopies spread above,
and golden bells and flowers [hanging therefrom].
Surrounding drapery hangs down;
his bodily color is pure and beautiful,
and his upright appearance is peerless.
His hair was deep blue-black;
his eyes were like bright stars;
and his nose was like a slice of polished copper.
His mouth was as if containing vermilion;
from the pores of his body issued the fragrance of *utpala* flowers;

Within the city of Sudarśana, the celestial palaces of the devas are immeasurable in number,
filling its center; its streets, avenues,
and thoroughfares are laid out in orderly divisions.
The rows of trees face one another;
along the paths, the precious trees stand stem to stem, gazing at each other.
At the bottom of the Xiáqú River, sunken incense is spread;
various birds frolic about,

They produce exquisite melodies of the *gong* and *shang* notes.
In those various palaces, ponds, streams, flowering trees, towers, pavilions, halls, and gardens along the pools,

What are the eight qualities?
First, it is light.
Second, cool;
third, warm;
fourth, beautiful.

It spread over the surface of the water;

By practicing the five precepts, the ten wholesome actions, and the four dhyānas, one fully attains rebirth therein.

By practicing the five precepts, the ten wholesome paths of action, and the four dhyānas, one fully attains rebirth therein.

By merely thinking of food, they are satiated.

By mindfulness of food, one is immediately satiated.

The bodies of those people are like the form of an intermediate state (antarābhava).
This is called the "Small Non-action" (parītta-asaṃskṛta), which is the highest worldly attainment.
Those who are attached to pleasure are difficult to transform;

Knowing the exhaustion [of outflows], practicing the path, and understanding the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, one attains liberation from the three realms;

Extending downward to the limit of the wind-circle and upward to the heaven of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,

Counting from one small world-system up to a thousand small world-systems,

A thousand of these small chiliocosms combined constitute one [medium chiliocosm];
thus, from one small chiliocosm, the count proceeds up to a thousand.

from one trichiliocosm, one counts up to a thousand worlds.

The thickness is likewise the same.
It encircles the small chiliocosm,
and its middle iron perimeter mountains rise as high as the eleventh heaven.
The thickness is likewise the same.

The thickness is likewise the same.

The thickness is likewise the same.
It encompasses a great trichiliocosm,

There are seven tiers of precious mountains and the waters of the great ocean, containing eight billion small continents.

Within the Lesser Iron Ring Mountains, the distance from east to west is one hundred and eighty million *li*,

All the myriad things under heaven are entirely contained therein.
Outside the four sides of the Cakravāḍa Mountains,

The four continents together comprise nine hundred billion hells,

If a person, with a heightened state of mind, commits the ten evil deeds, [they fall into them].

Those who commit the ten evil deeds to a middling degree [are subject to this].
One undergoes punishment within the thirty-six hells before finally being able to emerge from them;

It is eight thousand yojanas in length and breadth,

Vomiting poisonous fire that fills the city of Avīci,

It filled the interior;

Among those in the world, there are naturally some deluded sentient beings who commit the five heinous crimes.
Killing one's father, killing one's mother, killing one's teacher, killing an arhat, shedding the blood of a Buddha,
destroying a Buddha’s stūpa or monastery, disrupting the harmony of the Saṃgha,
stealing property, and slandering the Vaipulya sūtras.
By slandering the Buddhas of the ten directions and violating the causes and effects of the precepts,
one commits such grave offenses of immediate retribution (*ānantarya*).
At the end of that person's life, they shall enter the Avīci Hell.
It is like an arrow shot that, throughout incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*),
endures all manner of sufferings without any rest.
Therefore, it is named the Avīci Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering.
One day and one night in that hell is equivalent to sixty minor kalpas by the reckoning of days, months, and years in the human world today.
Thus they undergo punishment for eighty-four thousand great kalpas before finally emerging;
they then enter eighteen hells in the eastern direction.
It is likewise in the south, west, and north.
Throughout all ninety hells,
they dwell within each individual hell for billions of years.
Only then can they escape,
yet they fall again among the animals—
among elephants, horses, oxen, sheep, donkeys, camels, dogs, pigs, hawks, owls, ducks, and geese— for tens of millions of years.
By offering their flesh to others,
they exhaust the retribution for their offenses;
only after emerging from the animal realm can they become human beings.
Furthermore, for five hundred lifetimes they were slaves and servants,
never attaining independence.
Furthermore, when born as a human, one will be poor and lowly;
their clothing will not cover their body,
and their food will not suffice for their mouth.
Furthermore, after five hundred lifetimes, one may again become human, yet this falls short of the [ideal] sequence.
For these reasons, a human body is difficult to obtain,
and an appearance of a Buddha in the world is difficult to encounter.
A Buddha’s appearance in the world is difficult to encounter;
the hearing of the sutras and Dharma is difficult to attain;
and meeting with the Sangha is difficult to find.
An enlightened teacher is difficult to encounter;
having obtained a human body and met a Buddha to hear the Dharma,
one should first apply oneself with earnest diligence to practicing the Path.
It is difficult to guard one’s body, speech, and mind; be careful not to be negligent.
For those who are negligent, once the root of humanity is lost, they will not be restored for ten thousand kalpas.
This is most difficult, most difficult.
Furthermore, they may again obtain human birth.
Regarding what is called a *kalpa*: from the beginning to the end of heaven and earth is termed one *kalpa*.
There are three grades of *kalpas*.
What are the three categories?
First is the great kalpa.
There is a great city.
It is one hundred and twenty *li* in length, breadth, and height.
It is filled to the brim with mustard seeds.
After a hundred years have passed, a human or a celestial being takes out a single mustard seed and sets it aside.
When a great city is thus completely emptied, it is called one great kalpa.
The lifespan of the devas in the realm of form is eighty-four million such kalpas;
only then does their life come to an end.
As for the intermediate kalpa:
there was a great city,
eighteen li in length, breadth, and height.
A large city is filled to the brim with mustard seeds.
After a hundred years have passed, a person takes one mustard seed and sets it aside.
When all the mustard seeds in this way have been exhausted, it is called an intermediate kalpa (antarakalpa).
The devas of the form realm count their lifespan by these units;
after one kalpa, two kalpas, up to a maximum of 130,672 kalpas,
they finally pass away.
As for a small kalpa:
there was a great city,
forty li in length, breadth, and height.
A large city is filled to the brim with mustard seeds.
After a hundred years have passed for humans and devas, one takes out a single mustard seed and sets it aside.
When all the seeds in this way have been removed from the great city, that period is called a small kalpa.
These are called the three grades of kalpas.
Furthermore, the gods of the four formless abodes in the formless realm delight in the bliss of cessation.
Next are the twenty-two heavens of the form realm,
which delight in the bliss of meditative concentration.
Next are the six heavens of the desire realm.
They delight in the pleasures of the five desires.
Although the three realms possess such pleasures, they still cannot escape destruction by the three calamities.
What are these three calamities?
First is the calamity of fire;
second is the calamity of water;
third is the calamity of wind.
When a minor kalpa (antarakalpa) ends, seven suns appear simultaneously, incinerating heaven and earth;
because all six heavens are utterly consumed, it is called a "calamity of fire.
When a middle kalpa (asankhyeyakalpa) ends, calamitous rains descend from the heavens.
It is as large as a chariot wheel;
after a period of hundreds of millions of years,
its waters surge up to a height reaching the twenty-fourth heaven.

Again, after passing through hundreds of millions of billions of years, [he traversed] all the great trichiliocosms, dichiliocosms, and chiliocosms containing the Iron Ring Mountains (Cakravāḍa) of the Form Realm and Desire Realm;
the sevenfold mountain ranges of precious jewels; the four continents; Mount Sumeru; and the twenty-four celestial palaces.
All things rot and decay;
this is called the calamity of water.
At the end of a great kalpa, a malignant wind arises.
He blew upon the three thousandfold great chiliocosm, including ten billion Iron Ring Mountains, ten billion Sumeru Kings of Mountains, and ten billion palaces of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven,
so that the mountains struck one another until they were reduced to nothing but fine dust, with not a single remnant left behind.
The three-thousandfold world system becomes entirely empty and desolate;

this is called the calamity of wind. It is stated in the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra* (Great Collection Sutra), in one hundred and twenty fascicles, that it explains in detail the matters within the world system.
The Great Sūtra is difficult to perceive;
therefore, this is merely a brief summary of its essential points.
Jambudvīpa is equal in length and breadth.
It measures three hundred and twenty thousand *li*.
This total includes its mountains, hills, rivers, and marshes; hence it is so.
It is proclaimed that the land of Pyŏngyang is twenty-eight hundred thousand *li* in circumference;
within it, there are sixteen great kingdoms in total.
It governed eighty-four thousand cities and comprised eight great kings and four celestial sons.
In the east was the Celestial Son of the State of Jin.
The population was flourishing.
To the south, there was a kingdom of India where the land abounded in elephants.
To the west is the Son of Heaven of the Great Qin country;
its land abounds in gold, silver, jade, and precious stones.
To the north is the Son of Heaven of the Yuezhi country.
The land abounds in fine horses.
Within this Jambudvīpa, there are sixteen trillion soldiers,
gathered in eighty-four thousand assemblies.
Within the earth there are six thousand four hundred kinds of people,
ten trillion types of fish,
and six thousand four hundred kinds of birds.
There are four thousand five hundred kinds of wild animals;
there are two thousand four hundred kinds of seas;
and within the seas, there are generally eight thousand kinds of grasses.
There are seven hundred and forty kinds of miscellaneous medicines,
forty kinds of incense,
and one hundred and twenty kinds of authentic jewels.
Within the ocean there are two thousand five hundred countries and one hundred and eighty small countries;
five hundred of these three hundred countries consume the five sounds.
There were five great kings who consumed fish, turtles, soft-shelled turtles, and crocodiles.
The first great king ruled over five hundred small states;
his name was Śrī.
When the kingdom was exhausted, did the Buddha have few affairs with the assembly?
The second king also ruled over five hundred small kingdoms;
his name was Kāla.
The land produces the seven treasures.
The third king likewise rules over five hundred small kingdoms;
his name is Bala.
The land produced forty-two kinds of jewels as well as a hundred pieces of lapis lazuli.
The fourth king also ruled over five hundred minor kingdoms,
and the fifth king likewise ruled over one hundred minor kingdoms.
The people within the five great cities are mostly dark-skinned, short, and small in stature.
The distance between these five great cities is six million five hundred thousand li.
Beyond these various kingdoms, there is only the salt ocean and no human inhabitants.
It is one million four hundred thousand li from Mount Cakravāḍa.
